newsitem.title: USA: Connecticut jobless rate up slightly in October.
newsitem.headline: Connecticut jobless rate up slightly in October.

text.p: Connecticut's unemployment rate rose slightly during October to 5.0 percent, the state Labor Department said Tuesday.
Non-farm jobs fell by 2,900 last month to 1,583,200, but that was up from 1,568,000 in October 1995 for an increase of 15,200 year to year.

An estimated 87,600 Connecticut residents were unemployed in October. That figure was up 2,700 from September, but down 7,800 from the same period the previous year. Connecticut's unemployment rate was two-tenths of a percentage point below the national rate of 5.2 percent.

Job losses were reported in most sectors: 2,000 in services; 800 in construction and mining; 400 in manufacturing; and 400 in finance, insurance and real estate. One hundred jobs were lost in transportation, communications and utilities. Increases of 400 jobs were reported in both the government and trade sectors.

"Despite the lower estimates of jobs in October, we shouldn't look at one month's data as an indication of any kind of trend," Salvatore DiPillo, labor statistics supervisor, said. He cited the state's job gains over the past two years, and the occasional dips that have occurred during that period.
"We may be beginning to see an improved economy and the coming holiday season attracting new jobseekers who have not yet obtained employment," DiPillo said.
Average weekly initial unemployment claims increased by 113 over the month to 4,247, but were down 626, or 12.8 percent from the previous year.
The manufacturing production workweek, not seasonally adjusted, averaged 42.8 hours, down three-tenths of an hour from the revised Septemeber figure.

Average hourly earnings, also unadjusted, were up two cents compared with the revised September figure, increasing to $14.10, and up 47 cents over the year. The resulting average weekly wage, at $603.48, was down $3.37 for the month, and up $10.57 over the year.
